content:
Marta: Quick heads-up: during a midflight model swap we saw fragment repetition (same seq id) on an active stream.
Ajay: Graceful preempt or immediate cut?
Marta: Graceful handoff to fallback model. Sometimes client got duplicate chunks.
Sam: Any duplicate upstream calls visible?
Marta: Single upstream call in logs. Dups look internal to edge.
Neel: Likely race: preempt wins before checkpoint persisted -> resume replays same seq.
Ajay: Options: delay preempt until soft-checkpoint flush (adds tail-latency) or issue a "seq-claim" (tombstone) on preempt so <=claim get dropped.
Sam: Seq-claim is low-latency but only safe for non-side-effect streams. Tool-calls need conservative behavior.
Marta: Proposed route flag: `resume.seq_claim_allowed: boolean` default false. If true we tombstone on preempt.
Neel: Add metrics: `edge.resume.seq_claims`, `edge.resume.duplicates_dropped`. Also make resume token binding atomic with last-acked seq.
Ajay: Short-term implement seq-claim for read-only routes, fall back to drain for side-effectful routes. Long-term: app-level idempotency keys.
Marta: I'll open a tiny RFC + test that injects preempt mid-stream and asserts no duplicate client-visible outputs for read-only routes.
Sam: Sounds good.
Marta: Thanks — will post PR link.
